_about: Donnelly's fourth monetary-policy sub-driver: does the central bank prefer a weaker or stronger currency? This is judgment, not data — no feed can supply it. Each entry is a stance (-1 wants weaker / 0 indifferent / +1 wants stronger or resists weakness), the evidence for it, and the date it was last reviewed. Edit freely; the page shows it as an opinion with its date.

USD.label: indifferent
USD.note: No exchange-rate objective. Treasury owns dollar policy; the 'strong dollar' line is rhetorical. The dollar is a by-product of rates and risk, not a target.

EUR.label: leans against strength
EUR.note: Officials flagged euro appreciation as a disinflationary risk in 2025 as EUR/USD approached 1.20; not a target, but strength above that area draws comment and weighs on the rate path.

JPY.label: resists weakness
JPY.note: Tolerates a weak yen in normal times but the Ministry of Finance intervened repeatedly in 2024 above 155–160 and jawbones below that. Policy normalisation is itself a yen-supportive stance.

GBP.label: indifferent
GBP.note: No stated preference; sterling moves are discussed only through their inflation pass-through.

CHF.label: leans against strength
CHF.note: The clearest case in G10: decades of intervention and negative rates to cap the franc, rates back at zero in 2025, explicit willingness to intervene if strength threatens the inflation target.

AUD.label: indifferent
AUD.note: Floats freely; the RBA comments on the currency only as a terms-of-trade and inflation channel.

CAD.label: indifferent
CAD.note: No preference expressed; the currency is treated as an outcome of oil and the Fed–BoC differential.

NZD.label: indifferent
NZD.note: Free float; intervention capacity exists but has not been used in over a decade.

NOK.label: mildly prefers stronger
NOK.note: Repeatedly cited krone weakness as a reason inflation stayed high in 2023–25 and kept rates higher for longer partly on that account; oil-fund FX purchases are a separate, mechanical flow.

SEK.label: prefers stronger
SEK.note: Said plainly in 2023 that the krona was too weak and that it was a problem for inflation; hedged part of its FX reserves to that end. The preference has softened as inflation fell but has not reversed.

CNY.label: manages, resists weakness
CNY.note: Managed float via the daily fix. Through 2024–25 the fix sat consistently stronger than models implied, capping depreciation; the bank also leans against fast appreciation. Stability, not a level, is the objective.

INR.label: smooths, resists weakness
INR.note: Heavy two-way intervention from a large reserve stock; the rupee is among the least volatile EM currencies by design. Tolerance for gradual depreciation, resistance to disorderly moves.

KRW.label: resists weakness at extremes
KRW.note: Smoothing operations and verbal intervention when the won weakens past roughly 1,400 per dollar; the National Pension Service FX swap line is used the same way.

BRL.label: resists disorderly weakness
BRL.note: Spot and swap interventions during the 2024 sell-off; very high real rates are set for inflation, but the bank clearly dislikes a real that falls fast.

MXN.label: indifferent
MXN.note: The FX Commission (Banxico + Finance Ministry) intervenes only in disorder; the peso is otherwise a pure rates-and-risk currency.
